core.title: Model a diverging journey as a flow router: a declared artifact-keyed registry selecting the next linear user/system flow
core.given: A planned journey diverges: which user/system flow runs next depends on an artifact produced earlier.
core.when: The planner decomposes the journey into user/system flows and records how the branch is routed.
core.then: Declare the branch as a flow router: a domain-owned, schema-valid routing registry (artifact_urn -> user_system_flow_id) keyed by the produced artifact (the divergence signal), composing strictly-linear user/system flows into a branching journey-of-journeys.
prefer: Key dispatch by one produced artifact URN; a composite (urn, discriminant) key is exceptional (planner.user-system-flow.dispatch-map-is-registry, planner.user-system-flow.dispatch-composite-key-exceptional).
Keep user/system flows linear; branch between user/system flows, in the flow router (planner.user-system-flow.linearity).
Name only the routing decision; leave the route-control runner and dispatcher to the coder/tester layers.
avoid: Expressing the dispatch map as code or an imperative map.
Specifying runner/dispatcher mechanics in planner artifacts.
Treating this definition as an enforced check; enforcement lives in the constraint/rule nodes that require it.
core.why: A flow router gives a diverging journey a stable meaning: the routing decision is a declared, artifact-keyed registry rather than branching inside user/system flows, so user/system flows stay linear.
evidence: Reviewer finds, for each divergence point in a journey, a declared registry entry artifact_urn -> user_system_flow_id owned by the domain and valid against its schema.
Reviewer confirms each user/system flow composed by the flow router is linear (no internal branching).
Any composite (urn, discriminant) key is justified as exceptional per planner.user-system-flow.dispatch-composite-key-exceptional.

Compliance is established transitively through the enforceable constraint/rule nodes that require this anchor (e.g. planner.user-system-flow.dispatch-map-is-registry, planner.user-system-flow.dispatch-composite-key-exceptional, planner.user-system-flow.linearity); this node has no validator of its own.
verification: Advisory semantic anchor, not an enforced check: this node binds to no validator and produces no direct findings of its own; compliance is established only transitively, through the enforceable constraint/rule conventions that require this anchor.

Reviewer applies the term decomposition of the anchor: flow router = routing-decision (selects the next user/system flow when a journey diverges, never branching inside a user/system flow; user/system flows stay linear), artifact-keyed (dispatch keyed by a produced artifact URN; a composite (urn, discriminant) key is exceptional), declared-registry (a declared, schema-valid, domain-owned registry, not code), user/system-flow-composing (sequences multiple linear user/system flows into a branching journey-of-journeys).
The check does not cover the runtime realization: the route-control runner and its dispatcher are governed by the coder/tester (implementation and test) conventions, not by this node.

facts.note: Task text names a branching journey or user/system flow routing.
Planner artifacts that declare user/system flows and their dispatch; a file-kind cue alone is not sufficient activation.

values: journey gains a divergence point / branch between user/system flows
facts.note: Whether a journey actually diverges is a semantic judgment over the plan; no detector exists (this node is an advisory anchor bound to no validator).

fires: Planner decomposes a journey whose next step depends on which artifact was produced (one outcome continues to one user/system flow, another outcome to a different user/system flow).
Planner authors or edits a dispatch map that selects a user/system flow from a produced artifact URN.
Planner is tempted to add a conditional branch inside a user/system flow to handle a diverging journey.
doesNotFire: A strictly linear journey that is fully served by a single user/system flow with no divergence.
Coder/tester work implementing the route-control runner or its dispatcher (runtime realization, governed by coder/tester conventions).
Plans that do not involve user/system flows or journey routing at all.

neutralityNotes: This convention is a planning-methodology definition with no stack constructs (no runtime, language, framework, path or suffix), so the core is nearly identical to the Bun text. Two residual non-neutralities: (1) the only Bun-only content is the legacy atdd.extension.coder/train-interlocking and atdd.extension.tester.train-interlocking node ids in verifier_detail[2], kept in bunOnly while the core says generically 'coder/tester conventions'; (2) citations of sibling conventions (planner.train.dispatch-map-is-registry, planner.train.dispatch-composite-key-exceptional, planner.train.linearity) are kept verbatim on the assumption the planner convention corpus is shared across stacks; a stack that renames those nodes must re-instantiate the citations. No profileRequirements are asserted: bun.json fixes no concrete URN shape, plan-artifact file kind, path or tool for this rule (it is an advisory anchor bound to no validator), so there is no exact Bun value to bind to a vocabulary key; at instantiation time urn.<artifact> and roles.plan_artifact.kinds from the stack's profile supply what an artifact URN and a plan artifact look like.
